mcqs.q: The epithelium of the buccal mucosa is:
opts: Non-keratinized stratified squamous with few short, blunt rete ridges
mcqs.explain: The buccal mucosa (lining mucosa) has a non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with few short, blunt rete ridges.

mcqs.q: The submucosa of the buccal mucosa contains:
opts: Fat cells and minor salivary glands
mcqs.explain: The buccal submucosa contains fat cells and minor salivary glands; the lamina propria is vascular.

mcqs.q: The lamina propria of the buccal mucosa is described as:
mcqs.explain: The lamina propria of the buccal mucosa is vascular connective tissue.

mcqs.q: The three zones of the lip, from inside out, are:
opts: Mucous (labial) side → vermilion border → skin side
mcqs.explain: The lip passes from the mucous (labial) side, through the vermilion border, to the skin side.

mcqs.q: The mucous (labial) side of the lip is composed of:
opts: Epithelium and lamina propria (with minor salivary glands)
mcqs.explain: The labial mucosa is composed of epithelium and lamina propria, and its submucosa contains minor salivary glands.

mcqs.q: The vermilion border is red because of:
opts: Tall connective-tissue papillae with capillaries beneath thin keratinized epithelium
mcqs.explain: At the vermilion border, tall vascular (capillary-filled) papillae show through a thin keratinized epithelium, giving the red colour.
The vermilion border lacks hair, sweat and (usually) salivary glands, so it tends to dry and crack.

mcqs.q: The skin side of the lip is composed of:
opts: Epidermis (epithelial layer) and dermis (dense connective tissue)
mcqs.explain: Skin is composed of the epidermis (epithelial layer) and the dermis (dense connective tissue layer).

mcqs.q: A structure found on the skin side of the lip but NOT in oral mucosa is the:
mcqs.explain: Hair follicles (with sebaceous and sweat glands) are present on the skin side but absent from oral mucosa.

mcqs.q: The gland associated with hair follicles, seen on the skin side of the lip, is the:
mcqs.explain: Sebaceous glands are associated with hair follicles on the skin side; sweat glands are also present.

mcqs.q: The coiled gland in the dermis that produces sweat is the:
mcqs.explain: Sweat glands are coiled glands in the dermis of the skin side of the lip; they are not found in oral mucosa.

mcqs.q: The few rete ridges in buccal mucosa are described as:
mcqs.explain: Buccal (lining) mucosa has only a few short, blunt rete ridges, unlike the tall ridges of masticatory mucosa.

mcqs.q: Minor salivary glands keep the lining mucosa moist and are located in the:
mcqs.explain: Minor salivary glands lie in the submucosa of the buccal and labial mucosa, keeping the surface moist.

mcqs.q: Compared with the buccal mucosa, the skin side of the lip is:
mcqs.explain: The skin side has a keratinized epidermis with hair follicles, sebaceous and sweat glands; the buccal mucosa is non-keratinized and moist.

mcqs.q: Which sequence correctly describes the surface covering from inside the mouth to the face on the lip?
mcqs.explain: From the oral cavity outward: labial mucosa, then the vermilion border, then skin.

mcqs.q: On a buccal mucosa slide, identifying minor salivary glands and fat in the submucosa confirms it is:
mcqs.explain: Non-keratinized epithelium with blunt rete ridges and a submucosa containing fat and minor salivary glands is characteristic of lining mucosa (buccal).

saqs.q: Describe the histology of the buccal mucosa.
saqs.a: Epithelium: non-keratinized stratified squamous with few short, blunt rete ridges. Lamina propria: vascular. Submucosa: fat cells and minor salivary glands.

saqs.q: Name the three zones of the lip.
saqs.a: Mucous (labial) side, vermilion border, and skin side.

saqs.q: Why is the vermilion border red?
saqs.a: Thin keratinized epithelium over tall connective-tissue papillae containing capillaries, which show through; it lacks glands.

saqs.q: What is the skin side of the lip composed of?
saqs.a: Epidermis (epithelial layer) and dermis (dense connective tissue), with hair follicles, sebaceous and sweat glands.

saqs.q: Which adnexal structures are found on the skin side but not in oral mucosa?
saqs.a: Hair follicles, sebaceous glands and sweat glands.

saqs.q: How is the labial mucosa structurally simpler than skin?
saqs.a: Labial mucosa = epithelium + lamina propria (no epidermis/dermis split, no hair/sweat/sebaceous glands); it is kept moist by minor salivary glands.
